Surah At-Tahrim (The Prohibition)

Madani; its verses are twelve.

﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what God has made lawful for you?﴾ It is related that the Prophet (ﷺ) was alone with Mariyah on the day of 'Aisha, and Hafsah came to know of it. He said to her: "Keep it secret for me. I have forbidden Mariyah to myself, and I give you good news that Abu Bakr and 'Umar will rule the affairs of my community after me." So she informed 'Aisha with it, and the two of them were close friends. It is also said: he was alone with her on the day of Hafsah, and he pleased her with that and asked her to keep it secret, but she did not keep it secret, so he divorced her and withdrew from his wives. Then Jibril (peace be upon him) descended and said: "Take her back, for she is one who fasts often and stands in prayer at night, and she is among your wives in Paradise." It is also related that he (peace be upon him) drank honey in the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh, and 'Aisha and Hafsah conspired and said: "We smell the odor of maghafir from you." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) disliked the smell of the *tufl*, so he prohibited the honey, and then this was revealed. Its meaning: why do you prohibit what God has made lawful for you, of the possession of the right hand, or of the honey?

﴿seeking the pleasure of your wives﴾ This is either an explanation of "you prohibit," or a circumstantial clause (*hal*) referring to its subject, or a resumptive sentence explaining what prompted it, indicating that this is not befitting for you.

﴿And God is Forgiving﴾ exceedingly forgiving; He has forgiven you this slip.

﴿Merciful﴾ He has had mercy on you and did not hold you accountable for it; He only reproved you in defense of your infallibility (*'ismah*).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 66, verse 2:

﴿Indeed, Allah has ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾. That is: He has prescribed for you their dissolution (tahlil), which is the undoing of what you have bound by means of expiation (kaffarah) or by an immediately attached exception (istithna'), so that one does not break the oath (yahnath). The first is what is intended here.

﴿And Allah is your Mawla﴾: your master (sayyid) and the one who manages your affairs.

﴿And He is the All-Knowing﴾ of what sets you right, so He prescribes it for you.

﴿the All-Wise﴾: the one who is precise in His acts and rulings, so He does not command you or forbid you except in accordance with what wisdom requires.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 66, verse 3:

﴿And when the Prophet confided a matter to one of his wives﴾, namely Hafsah.

﴿a statement﴾, i.e., the matter of the prohibition regarding Mariyah, or the honey, or the matter of the caliphate.

﴿Then when she disclosed it﴾, i.e., Hafsah informed 'A'ishah of the statement and divulged it to her. It is also read as "anba'at bihi" (she informed of it).

﴿and Allah made him aware of it﴾, i.e., Allah the Exalted informed the Prophet (ﷺ) of Hafsah's disclosure.

﴿He made known part of it﴾, i.e., the Prophet (ﷺ) made known to Hafsah part of the statement she had disclosed. It is said that this was the matter of the caliphate (imamah). It is narrated that he (ﷺ) said to her: "Did I not tell you to keep it secret from me?" She said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, I could not contain myself out of joy at the honour which Allah the Exalted had bestowed upon her father."

﴿and he ignored part of it﴾, i.e., he refrained, out of generosity, from making known part of it. It is said that this was the matter of Mariyah.

﴿Then when he informed her of it﴾, i.e., the Prophet (ﷺ) informed Hafsah of what he had learned of the statement.

﴿She said: "Who told you this?"﴾, i.e., of her disclosure of the statement.

﴿He said: "The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me"﴾, the One from whom nothing hidden is concealed.

﴿If you two turn in repentance to Allah﴾: a direct address to Hafsa and 'A'isha, using iltifat (a shift from one grammatical form to another, here from the third person to the second) to add emphasis to the reproach.

﴿For your hearts have inclined﴾: the fa' here is for ta'lil (causal explanation), as in the line of verse, "Worship your Lord, for worship is a duty." The meaning is: what requires repentance has already occurred from you both, namely the inclining of your hearts away from what is obligatory for you, which is sincere devotion to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), loving what he loves, and disliking what he dislikes. It is also read as "fa-qad zaghat qulubukuma" (your hearts have swerved).

﴿And if you back each other up against him﴾: with one of the two tā' letters dropped. It is also read in its original form, and with the zā' doubled and tazhara (you two support one another). The meaning is: you cooperate against him in ways that distress him, such as excessive interference with others and disclosing his secret.

﴿Then indeed Allah is his protector, and Jibril, and the righteous among the believers﴾: meaning, he will never lack someone who supports him. Allah is his helper, Jibril is the chief of the Karubiyyin (the cherubim) and his companion, and whoever among the believers is righteous are his followers and helpers. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: by "the righteous among the believers" he meant Abu Bakr and 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both). This has been related as a marfu' (traced directly to the Prophet ﷺ), and 'Ikrima and Muqatil also said so. This is the most fitting reading, given its position between Jibril and the angels (peace be upon them), for it combines the moral backing and the outward backing. How could it not be? Jibril is a supporter of him (peace be upon them both), supporting him with Divine aid, and these two are his ministers and supporters in managing the affairs of the message and carrying out its outward rulings. Moreover, the declaration of their backing of him (peace and blessings be upon him) has a stronger effect on the hearts of their two daughters and weakens their position. Thus it deserves precedence, unlike the case where the phrase is taken to mean the category of righteous people in general, which is the well-known view.

﴿And the angels﴾: despite their great number and the filling of the heavens with their hosts.

﴿after that﴾: it has been said: that is, after the support of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His greatest confidant (na-mus, the one entrusted with the secret), and the righteous among the believers.

﴿are a supporting band﴾: that is, a company that backs him, as though they were one hand against whoever opposes him. What then is the benefit of the support of two women against those whose supporters are these? What is indicated by the words of the Exalted, ﴿after that﴾, is the excellence of their support over the support of others, since the support of all of them is the support of Allah the Exalted, and His support through them and their backing is superior to all other forms of His support. This is what they have said. But the more fitting view is that "that" (dhalika) be understood as referring specifically to the backing of the righteous among the believers, and that the statement of the subsequent backing by the angels serves as a correction of what the order of mention might suggest about the superiority of what was mentioned first. It is as if it were said: after mentioning the backing of the righteous among the believers and the rest of the angels, after that is a supporter for him (peace and blessings be upon him), signifying the high rank of their backing, the lofty station of their position, and the restoration of their distinction from the backing of Jibril (peace be upon him).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 66, verse 5:

﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you﴾. That is, He will give him (peace be upon him) wives in place of you. (p-268) ﴿Wives better than you﴾ is either by way of taghlib (the grammatical device of giving precedence to one group within a mixed address, here the masculine plural over the feminine) or by generalizing the address. There is nothing in it indicating that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) did not divorce Hafsah, or that there are women better than them, since making the divorce of all of them conditional does not contradict divorcing one of them. And what is conditioned on something that has not occurred does not necessarily have to occur. It was also recited as "أنْ يُبَدِّلَهُ" with the shaddah (doubling of the letter ب, making it "yubaddilahu").

﴿Muslim (submissive), believing, devout, obedient, repentant, worshipful, and fasting (or emigrating)﴾ with the following explanations:

﴿Muslimat﴾ means affirming and sincere, or submitting and believing.

﴿Qanitat﴾ means praying, or persevering in obedience.

﴿Ta'ibat﴾ means repenting from sins.

﴿Abidat﴾ means devoting oneself to worship, or humbly submitting to the command of the Messenger (ﷺ).

﴿Sa'ihat﴾ means fasting. The one who fasts is called sa'ih (wanderer) because he moves about during the day without provisions. Or it means emigrating (muhajirat). It was also recited as "سِيحاتٍ".

﴿Thayyibat wa abkaran﴾ (previously married and virgins). The conjunction (al-'atif, the connecting "wa") was placed between them because the two are mutually exclusive.

﴿O you who believe, protect yourselves﴾ by abandoning acts of disobedience and performing acts of obedience.

﴿and your families﴾ by making them take on the same obligations you take on for yourselves. It is also read as "أهلوكم" (ahlūkum), coordinated with the waw in "قوا" (qū, "protect"). In that case "أنفسكم" (anfusakum) is an expression for the selves of everyone, by way of giving precedence to the addressees (taghlīb al-mukhāṭabīn), meaning: "protect yourselves, and let your families protect their selves."

﴿a Fire whose fuel is men and stones﴾ That is, a fire kindled by them both, kindled just as other fires are kindled by firewood. He commanded the believers to guard against this Fire, which is prepared for the disbelievers, as is stated in Surah al-Baqarah, in order to intensify the warning.

﴿Over it are angels﴾ That is, they are in charge of it and of punishing its people, and they are the Zabaniyah (the guardians of Hell).

﴿harsh and severe﴾ Harsh in speech and severe in deeds, or harsh in character and severe in creation, and strong in carrying out severe actions.

﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them﴾ That is, in His command, with "amarahu" understood as a substitute of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) for "Allah," or as "fī mā amarahum bihi" with the preposition removed (naza' al-khāfiḍ), meaning: they do not refuse to accept the command, and they hold themselves bound to it.

﴿and they do what they are commanded﴾ That is, they carry out what they are commanded to do without any reluctance or negligence.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 66, verse 7:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have disbelieved, do not make excuses today﴾ are a quotation (maqul) of a statement that has been omitted, relying on the confidence that the situation (dalalat al-hal) points to it. That is: it will be said to them, this, at the time the angels cause them to enter the Fire, in accordance with what they were commanded.

﴿You are only being recompensed for what you used to do﴾ in the world of disbelief and sins, after you were forbidden from them in the strongest terms and commanded to have faith and obedience, so there is absolutely no excuse for you.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 66, verse 8:

﴿O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance (tawbatan nasuhan)﴾ That is: reaching the utmost in sincerity (bali'atan fi al-nush). The repentance is described with this on the basis of metaphorical attribution (al-isnad al-majazi), which is the description of those who repent, namely that they give sincere advice (yansahu) to their own selves by repenting, and so they come with it in its proper manner. That is: they repent of vices because of their ugliness, regretful of them, deeply distressed (mughtammin ashadda al-ightimam) at having committed them, resolved that they will not return to any vice of the vices, settling their selves upon that such that no diverting thing turns them away from it at all.

On the authority of Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): repentance is comprised of six things: regret for past sins, repeating the obligatory acts (al-i'ada li-al-fara'id), restoring what was wrongfully taken (radd al-mazalim), seeking the forgiveness of those whom you wronged (istihlal al-khusum), resolving that you will not return, and melting your self in obedience to Allah the Exalted as you had nurtured it in disobedience, and making it taste the bitterness of obedience as you had made it taste the sweetness of disobedience.

And on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab: that one does not return even if one is cut with a sword and burned with fire. It was also said: "nasuhan" is from nasahat al-thawb (the mending of a garment), meaning a repentance that mends your tears in your religion and repairs your flaws. It was also said: "pure" (khalisa), from their saying "honey nasih" when it is purified of wax. It is also permissible that it means a repentance that gives advice to people, that is, it calls them to its like, because its effect is evident in its possessor and his use of earnestness and resolve in acting upon its requirements. It was read as "tawban nasuhan," and it was read as "nusuhan," which is the verbal noun of nusiha (nusuh), for nush and nusuh are like shukr and shukur. That is: possessing sincerity, or it gives sincere advice in full, or repent for the sake of the sincerity of your selves, with it being an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu).

﴿It may be that your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ The appearance of the form of hope (sigha al-ith'am) is in keeping with the customs of majesty (ala sunan al-kibriya') and an indication that it is an act of grace, and that repentance does not necessitate it, and that the servant ought to be between fear and hope even if he exaggerates in carrying out the duties of worship.

﴿On the day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet﴾ is an adverbial temporal clause (zarf) for "yudkhilukum" (He will admit you).

﴿And those who believed with him﴾ is a conjunction upon "the Prophet," and in it is an allusion to those whom Allah the Exalted disgraced from among the people of disbelief and wickedness, and a praise addressed to the believers, in that He preserved them from the likes of their condition. It was said: it is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿their light runs before them and on their right hands﴾, that is, upon the Sirat. On the first view this is a resumptive clause (isti'naf) or a circumstantial clause (hal), and likewise His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿they say﴾ ... etc. And on the second view it is another predicate for the relative (al-mawsul), that is: they say when the light of the hypocrites is extinguished.

﴿Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us, indeed You are Most Capable of all things﴾ It was said: they supplicate seeking nearness to Allah along with the completeness of their light. It was said: their lights vary according to their deeds, so they ask for its completion as an act of grace. It was said: those foremost to Paradise pass over the Sirat like lightning, and some like the wind, and some crawling and creeping; and those are the ones who say: ﴿Our Lord, perfect for us our light﴾.

O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers (﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ جاهِدِ الكُفّارَ﴾) with the sword.

And the hypocrites (﴿والمُنافِقِينَ﴾) with argument.

﴿And be harsh upon them﴾ (﴿واغْلُظْ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾): employ harshness toward both groups in what you strive against them with, of fighting and of disputation.

﴿And their refuge is Hell﴾ (﴿وَمَأْواهم جَهَنَّمُ﴾): they will see therein a severe punishment.

﴿And wretched is the destination﴾ (﴿وَبِئْسَ المَصِيرُ﴾): that is, Hell, or their destination.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 66, verse 10:

﴿Allah has set forth an example for those who disbelieve.﴾ The coining of an example (darb al-mathal, "striking a parable") in such contexts is an expression for presenting a strange situation so that another situation, similar to it in strangeness, may be known through it. That is: Allah has made an example (mathal) of the state of these disbelievers, their condition and their outcome. "Mathalan" is the second object of "daraba" (set forth), and the lam is connected to it. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot﴾, that is, their state, is the first object, which has been placed after the verb so that what explains and details their state may be joined to it, and thereby the state of these people becomes clear. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿they were under two of Our righteous servants﴾ is an explanation of their state that called them to goodness and righteousness, that is: they were in the marital bond of two prophets of great standing, able to attain the good of both this world and the Hereafter and to obtain their two felicities. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿but they betrayed them﴾ (p-270) is an explanation of the great offence that proceeded from them, while affirming what would negate it of companionship with the Prophet. That is: they betrayed them through disbelief and hypocrisy. This is a depiction of their state, which mirrors the state of these disbelievers in their betrayal of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ through disbelief and disobedience, despite their full capacity for faith and obedience. His saying, [exalted is He: ﴿so they did not avail them﴾ ... etc.] is an explanation of what their betrayal led to, that is: the two prophets did not avail them.

﴿against Allah﴾ regarding the right of marriage.

﴿anything﴾ that is, of any benefit.

﴿And it was said﴾ to them at their death, or on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿"Enter the Fire along with those who enter."﴾ That is: along with all the other disbelievers who enter it, those who have no connection between themselves and the prophets, upon them be peace.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 66, verse 11:

﴿And Allah has set forth an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh﴾. That is: He made her condition an example for the condition of the believers, in that the connection of the disbelievers does not harm them, since she was in the world under the most hostile of Allah's enemies, while she is in the highest chambers of Paradise. And His saying, exalted is He, ﴿when she said﴾ is an adverbial clause (zarf) governed by a deleted element to which reference is made, meaning: Allah set forth for the believers her condition, "when she said."

﴿My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise﴾ near Your mercy, or in the highest of the ranks of those brought near. It is narrated that when she said that, her house in Paradise was shown to her, made of a pearl, and her soul was taken.

﴿And save me from Pharaoh and his deeds﴾ That is: from his wicked self and his evil deeds.

﴿And save me from the wrongdoing people﴾ from the Copts who followed him in wrongdoing.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 66, verse 12:

﴿And Mary, daughter of 'Imran﴾ is conjoined to "the wife of Pharaoh," as consolation for widows. That is: God struck an example for those who believe, [namely] her state and what she was given of the honor of this world and the Hereafter, and of being chosen above the women of the worlds, despite her people being disbelievers.

﴿who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into it﴾. It is also read as "into her" (fīhā), meaning Mary.

﴿of Our spirit﴾: of a spirit that We created without any intermediary at all.

﴿and she affirmed the words of her Lord﴾: [the words] of His scriptures that were revealed, or [the words] of what He revealed to His prophets.

﴿and His books﴾: [she affirmed] all of His revealed books. It is also read as "the word of God" (bi-kalimati Allāh) and "His Book," meaning [she affirmed] 'Isa and the Book revealed to him, which is the Injil (Gospel).

﴿and she was among the devout (al-qānitīn)﴾: that is, among those who were constant in obedience. The masculine form is used for the predominance [of the masculine] (al-taghlīb), and it signals that her obedience did not fall short of the obedience of men, to the point that she was counted among them, or among their offspring, because she was from the descendants of Harun, brother of Musa, peace be upon them both.

From the Prophet (ﷺ): "Many men attained perfection, but among women only four attained perfection: Asiya daughter of Muzahim, Mary daughter of 'Imran, Khadija daughter of Khuwaylid, and Fatima daughter of Muhammad, may the blessings of God be upon him [and them]. And the excellence of 'A'isha over women is like the excellence of tharid over other foods."

And from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surat al-Tahrim, God will grant him sincere repentance (tawbatan naṣūḥan)."

The eighth part is complete, and it is followed by the ninth part, whose beginning is the surah
